about: The M0 families' tokenizer side files at their pinned revisions, by their testdata/fixtures.toml names, and the specials TokenizerSpec must extract from them (COMP-E17-T14; RFC-0043 §8.1). The expected IDs were read from the files by hand, apart from syntropy-manifest: tokenizer_config.json's bos_token, eos_token, pad_token and unk_token looked up in tokenizer.json's added_tokens, generation_config.json's eos_token_id, and the added tokens spelled <|fim_prefix|>, <|fim_middle|> and <|fim_suffix|>. chat_template_sha256 is SHA-256 over tokenizer_config.json's chat_template string as UTF-8. tokenizer_id is the TokenizerId syntropy-manifest computed from these files when they were recorded, pinned so a change to the files or to the ID's encoding shows. Both Qwen3 repositories ship byte-identical tokenizer files. Their tokenizer_config.json sets bos_token to null, so BOS is none, although generation_config.json has bos_token_id 151643: RFC-0043 §8.1 reads BOS from tokenizer_config.json only. The files were read on 2026-10-31 from the Hub at the pinned commits, checked against the Hub's sha256 or git blob id and against the manifest's BLAKE3 before use.
